jobs.title: Research Engineer
jobs.description:
Outset invented a better way to do research: AI-powered user interviews.

Global brands like Hubspot, Microsoft, Uber and Nestle use Outset to achieve deeper, qualitative insights about their users at unprecedented speed and scale.

The research industry is massive (>$140B and growing) and ripe for disruption. Incumbents are outdated, slow, and burdened by high-cost services. That's our opportunity.

Outset is backed by top Silicon Valley investors and raised a $30M Series B in December 2025—less than six months after our Series A—led by Radical Ventures with participation from M12 (Microsoft’s venture arm), 8VC, Y Combinator, and Adverb Ventures.

The raise follows a breakout year, with our business growing 8x as enterprise customers across industries adopt our category, AI‑moderated research, as the new standard for understanding people.

We’re a tight-knit team serving some of the world’s largest enterprises.

Outset builds digital twins: AI systems that represent specific real people and respond to research questions the way those people would. The Digital Twins Team runs an ongoing research program to measure and improve how faithfully these systems reproduce human responses and behavior, across a range of cross-sectional levels of analysis.

The Research Engineer reports to the Head Scientist and builds and maintains the systems that let the team's scientists run their studies correctly, reproducibly, and at scale. The scientists design the studies and define the measurements; you make sure every experiment executes exactly as designed, that results can be reproduced from stored inputs, and that research code stays in step with the shipped product. The ideal candidate has supported scientists in an academic computational social science lab or a comparable research setting and has hands-on experience engineering systems built on large language models.

**Responsibilities**

* Own the evaluation infrastructure that tests competing modeling approaches, so that new tests can be set up quickly, run concurrently and automatically, and be monitored.
* Implement measurement pipelines exactly as specified by the scientists, with deterministic and traceable outputs.
* Maintain versioned evaluation datasets with held-out sets that are never used for training.
* Build and maintain data pipelines for human-participant data, external datasets, and model training data, including linkage of records belonging to the same participant across sources.
* Keep research code in step with the production product so that validated improvements ship promptly.
* Detect and prevent threats to the validity of evaluations.
* Track compute and API spend across experiments and their implications for production-stage costs
* Manage repositories, code review, documentation, and the reproducibility of the team's coding workflow.
* Identify implementation choices that can be made more correct or more efficient, and propose changes.

**Qualifications**

* Several years of software engineering experience, including experience supporting researchers in a lab or comparable setting.
* Experience translating specific scientific requirements and experiment designs into code.
* Experience building and operating large-scale data pipelines on human behavior data, and confirming that the pipelines matched the criteria and design the researchers specified.
* Strong Python, including the ability to read and audit code produced by agentic coding tools.
* Fundamentals of computing: file systems, software libraries, databases, SQL, tabular data, and Git-based workflows.
* Experience with cloud infrastructure and with running many jobs concurrently.
* Working understanding of machine learning, including how transformer-based language models behave, how model APIs are used, and what fine-tuning involves.
* A habit of writing deterministic, reproducible, cost-aware, and well-documented code.

**Preferred**
-------------

* Hands-on experience engineering large language model systems: prompt pipelines, evaluation harnesses, embedding computation, agentic systems, and/or fine-tuning infrastructure.
* Experience fine-tuning open-weight language models on multi-GPU hardware.
* Experience serving open-weight models with an inference framework such as vLLM or SGLang, including batched inference and prefix caching for many requests that share a common prompt.
* Experience with experiment tracking and cost monitoring for machine learning workloads.
* Experience with survey or panel data and data collection platforms.
* Experience extracting and storing model activations for downstream analysis.
* Experience with experiment tracking and cost monitoring for machine learning workloads, including GPU provisioning across cloud providers.
* Prior work on generative agents, digital twins, or simulation of human respondents.

Compensation Range: $200K - $240K

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Algorithms
jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. You will develop the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it. The core challenge is rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip.

Your job is to develop the algorithms that exploit this natively: understand which parts of LLM workloads are best suited to in-memory execution, design numerical methods that map onto the hardware's physical behavior, and validate them against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.

This is a co-design role. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, which means you will influence architectural decisions rather than implement against a fixed specification. The strongest candidates have a deep understanding of both large model inference and the mathematics of stochastic systems, and have built systems that run on real hardware.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Algorithm Development:** Develop algorithms for LLM inference workloads running on our in-memory hardware. Success means algorithms that measurably improve LLM inference on our hardware, demonstrated in simulation and then on silicon.
* **Software/Hardware Co-Design:** Work directly with hardware and architecture teams to shape what the chip can and should compute natively.
* **Numerical Methods:** Design numerical methods that exploit thermal noise and analog dynamics rather than working around them.
* **Evaluation & Benchmarks:** Build evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that characterize algorithm behavior on real hardware or simulation.
* **Workload Translation:** Translate insights about model workloads into constraints and opportunities for hardware design.
* **Rapid Prototyping:** Prototype and iterate rapidly as hardware evolves from simulation to silicon.
* **Performance Optimization:** Optimize performance at both the gate level and the algorithmic level.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Deep understanding of large model inference: attention mechanisms, KV cache, long-context decoding, memory bandwidth constraints
* Experience with inference optimization: quantization, sparsity, kernel fusion, or memory-efficient attention
* Familiarity with stochastic systems, probabilistic methods, numerical analysis, or analog computation
* Experience implementing algorithms close to hardware, beyond high-level frameworks
* Comfort reasoning from first principles about what a novel substrate can do efficiently
* Track record of taking ideas from theory to working implementation on real hardware
* Strong programming skills in Python and at least one systems language
* Collaborative instinct and ability to work across hardware, architecture, and software teams

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* PhD in machine learning, applied mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, or a related field
* Exposure to analog or mixed-signal systems, in-memory compute, or non-von-Neumann architectures
* Experience working on hardware that did not yet exist when you joined
* Publications or open-source work in efficient inference, stochastic algorithms, or novel computing

**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Our compiler is how models reach that hardware, and new LLM architectures show up faster than most compilers can track. A new attention variant, MoE routing scheme, or quantization approach has to be represented faithfully in our compiler before it can run, let alone run fast. As a Compiler Engineer focused on frontend and model bring-up, you will extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes so new LLM architectures are supported before a customer asks for them.

This is a research-adjacent seat: you are expected to follow the literature closely, and publish on behalf of Normal. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will validate bring-up against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, so that models are ready to run when silicon arrives.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Model Bring-up**: Bring up frontend and mid-level support for new LLM architectures in our compiler, from attention variants to MoE routing schemes. Success means new architectures run correctly on our stack soon after release, ahead of customer demand.
* **IR and Lowering**: Extend our IR, ops, and lowering passes to represent new architectural primitives faithfully rather than approximately, with test coverage that keeps them correct as the compiler evolves.
* **Quantization and Numerics**: Represent the quantization schemes and numeric formats new models use, so lowering preserves model accuracy.
* **Architecture Tracking**: Track the LLM architecture landscape closely enough to recommend what the team brings up next.
* **Cross-Team Handoffs**: Hand lowered programs to the backend compiler engineers who map them onto our hardware, and work with our LLM serving engineer to take new models from compiler support to serving.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Hands-on ML compiler experience: you have written and shipped compiler passes
* Deep familiarity with PyTorch internals, ideally including its compilation stack (TorchDynamo, FX, torch.export)
* Working knowledge of modern LLM architectures at the level of attention mechanisms, MoE routing, and quantization schemes
* Patience for the unglamorous part of the job: getting a new architecture from “runs” to “runs correctly” to “runs correctly and fast”
* Comfort designing compiler infrastructure in a young codebase as well as extending an established one

* Familiarity with other ML frameworks and graph formats, such as JAX or ONNX
* Experience partitioning models across devices with tensor, pipeline, or expert parallelism
* Experience with hardware-software co-design
* Experience with non-standard or in-memory hardware targets

Building great software takes more than writing code. It takes teams working together, and too often, the information they need is scattered across tools, conversations, and systems.

PlayerZero is an AI platform that connects work across enterprise Support, Engineering, Product, QA, and SRE teams, helping them resolve issues faster, improve software quality, and plan what to build next.

Our agents (we call them Players :) use that context to take on work across the software lifecycle. They learn from each outcome, earning trust and taking on more responsibility over time.

Most AI tools help one person perform a task faster, a session at a time. But real software work doesn’t happen in one session or one tool. The most interesting context lives between those systems of record, and so does the real work.

* **Scale sandboxes and fleets.** An organization’s work is spread across laptops, QA fleets, production hosts, and ephemeral scripts. \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Position Summary**

We are seeking a Full Stack Engineer to build a centralized knowledge platform for our partner organizations — a single, role-aware entry point consolidating reporting, a strategy library, and operational applications into one product. We need a driven, curious, and innovative engineer focused on building systems for all NBA teams to leverage in driving revenue, efficiencies and fandom.

You will drive features end to end — interface, API, and the data behind them — in Python and modern JavaScript or TypeScript, Microsoft Azure, and AI semantic layers built on the Azure AI platform. This is a build-from-here role with a start-up character inside a large organization: reading unfamiliar systems, empowered decision making and creating institutional product knowledge as you build at scale.

  

**Major Responsibilities**

  

**PRODUCT ENGINEERING**

* Design, build, and ship features end to end — Nuxt-based interfaces, Python backend services deployed as Azure services, REST APIs, and the data models beneath them.
* Build search, tagging, and content discovery, including role-aware views that show each organization only what it should see.
Write and optimize SQL across the data ecosystem; build connectors and migration pipelines that move an enterprise document library into a structured, tagged repository at volume.  

  

**AZURE AI & SEMANTIC LAYER**

* Build AI semantic layer on the Azure AI platform — retrieval-augmented search and natural-language querying using Azure AI Search and Azure OpenAI models.
* Design the ingestion path that makes content retrievable: chunking, embedding, security trimming, and index maintenance.
Drive enablement of business skills, advanced analytics modeling, and fan activation tools within team business platforms.  

  

**PLATFORM & WAYS OF WORKING**

* Share ownership of Azure environments, CI/CD, monitoring, and enterprise identity integration with the engineering team.
* Work to engineering team standards — Git and code review, automated testing, containerized local development — and document features, data flows, and inherited configuration as you go.
Partner with product management and communicate clearly with non-technical colleagues across marketing, business operations, and analytics.  

  

**Required Education / Professional Experience**

* Bachelor's degree, or equivalent practical experience.
* Demonstrated experience shipping production web applications as part of an engineering team, including both user-facing interfaces and the services behind them.
Demonstrated experience building and running applications on Microsoft Azure, including at least one production workload using Azure AI services.  

  

**Required Skills / Knowledge Attributes**

* Hands-on experience with the Azure AI platform — Azure OpenAI Service, Azure AI Search, and Azure AI Foundry — used to build a retrieval-augmented or natural-language application that real users depend on. Depth here is a primary requirement of this role.
* Working command of the surrounding Azure stack: compute, storage, managed databases, secrets, and Microsoft Entra ID as a consumer of it.
* Proficiency in Python, and strong skills in TypeScript with a modern frontend framework.
* REST API design, and strong SQL against relational databases and cloud data platforms.
* Practical understanding of AI application patterns — RAG, embeddings and vector search, semantic layers, tool calling, evaluation, and grounding.
* Strong Git and collaborative development practice, including CI/CD and written documentation.
* Ability to work in an unfamiliar codebase and cloud environment: read it, extend it safely, and document what you find.
Comfort in an early-stage, start-up-style team — owning work independently and shaping process where none exists yet.  

  

**Preferred Skills / Knowledge Attributes**

* Experience at a start-up, or on a founding or early-stage product team.
* Azure certification — Azure AI Engineer Associate, Azure Developer Associate, or equivalent.
* Experience building a centralized knowledge platform, internal data portal, or enterprise search product, including permission-aware retrieval.
* Experience with semantic or metric layers over a data warehouse.
* Experience with Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, SharePoint and Microsoft Graph, or embedding BI content such as Tableau or Power BI with row- and role-level security.
Interest in or experience with sports business — ticketing, partnerships, marketing, or analytics.

$5,000 - $5,750 bi-weekly

jobs.description:
**About the Role**

Global Tempus Technologies is hiring a Cloud Infrastructure Engineer to build, maintain, and improve cloud environments that support business applications and services.

You’ll work on cloud infrastructure, deployment automation, security, and system reliability. The role involves developing infrastructure as code, supporting cloud migrations, and resolving technical issues that affect performance or availability.

We’re looking for an engineer with practical cloud experience who can automate routine work, troubleshoot infrastructure problems, and help keep systems secure and dependable.

**What You'll Do**

* Design, deploy, and maintain cloud infrastructure based on application and business requirements.
* Automate infrastructure provisioning, configuration, deployment, and routine operational tasks.
* Use infrastructure-as-code tools to manage environments consistently and repeatably.
* Monitor cloud services and investigate performance, availability, and capacity issues.
* Apply security controls and access-management practices to cloud resources.
* Support cloud migrations, including planning, implementation, testing, and troubleshooting.
* Work with software developers and operations teams to improve deployment processes.
* Maintain documentation for infrastructure configurations, procedures, and system changes.
* Identify opportunities to reduce manual work and improve operational efficiency.
* Troubleshoot infrastructure incidents and help determine their root causes.
* Support backup, recovery, and business continuity practices.
* Review infrastructure configurations for reliability, security, and scalability.
* Participate in technical reviews and recommend practical improvements to cloud architecture.

**What We're Looking For**

* Professional experience in cloud engineering, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or a related technical role.
* Practical knowledge of at least one major cloud platform, such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud.
* Experience with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, or comparable technologies.
* Familiarity with scripting or automation using languages such as Python, Bash, or PowerShell.
* Understanding of networking, identity and access management, storage, and compute services.
* Experience with monitoring, logging, troubleshooting, and incident response.
* Knowledge of cloud security practices and access controls.
* Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and version control systems such as Git.
* Ability to investigate technical problems and communicate findings clearly.
* Strong documentation, organisation, and problem-solving skills.
* A degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field is beneficial. Relevant practical experience may also be considered.

**What We Expect**

You should be able to identify infrastructure problems, assess their impact, and work through solutions methodically. Automation should be maintainable, infrastructure changes should be documented, and security should be considered throughout the development and deployment process.

You’ll also need to communicate effectively with developers and operations colleagues. When a migration, deployment, or infrastructure change introduces a risk, explain the issue clearly and work with the relevant team to resolve it.
